# nish\:async

Tasks for `async` functions: start one and go on, or await two to eight at once.

```ts
import {
  awaitAll,
  cancel,
  cancelAfter,
  cancelled,
  readable,
  readableWithin,
  sleep,
  spawn,
  taskId,
  writable,
  writableWithin,
} from "nish:async";
```

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { awaitAll, spawn } from "nish:async";

async function double(x: i32): Promise<i32> {
  return x * 2;
}

async function log(x: i32): Promise<void> {
  console.log(x);
}

async function run(): Promise<void> {
  const [c, d] = await awaitAll(double(1), double(2));
  spawn(log(c + d));
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="await​All" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#awaitall">

Wait for two calls at once.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="cancel" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#cancel">

Cancel a task: every `sleep`, `readable` or `writable` it is waiting on answers `false` at once, and so does every one it makes later, so it runs on to its end, its `using` bindings dispose and its region is freed.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="cancel​After" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#cancelafter">

Cancel a task `ms` milliseconds from now, unless it finishes first.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="cancelled" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#cancelled">

Whether the running task has been cancelled.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readable" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readable">

Suspend the task until `fd` has bytes to read, or its peer has hung up, while the executor runs the others.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="readable​Within" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#readablewithin">

Suspend the task until `fd` has bytes to read, or its peer has hung up, or `ms` milliseconds pass, whichever comes first.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="sleep" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#sleep">

Suspend the task for `ms` milliseconds while the executor runs the others.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="spawn" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#spawn">

Start `task` as a task of its own and go on without waiting for it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="task​Id" icon="phosphor/regular/function" href="#taskid">

The running task's handle, to hand to `cancel` or `cancelAfter`.

</scalar-card>

Suspend the task until `fd` takes bytes without blocking, while the executor runs the others.

</scalar-card>

Suspend the task until `fd` takes bytes without blocking, or `ms` milliseconds pass, whichever comes first.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>

<scalar-callout type="info">

All five are reached only through the import. Each argument to `awaitAll`
or `spawn` is a direct call to an `async` function, written where it is
made, which the checker holds it to (`src/async-check.ts`); `tsc` sees ordinary promises. A spawned
call's arguments are numbers, `boolean`s, enums or `string`s (NL2673): the
task outlives the function that spawned it.

</scalar-callout>

`sleep(ms)`, `readable(fd)` and `writable(fd)` are the waits a task makes
on the executor, an epoll (kqueue on Darwin) loop that resumes ready tasks
in the kernel's order and then expired timers by deadline:

<scalar-code-group>

```ts example.ts
import { readable, sleep } from "nish:async";

async function tick(): Promise<void> {
  await sleep(10);
  console.log("tick");
}
```

</scalar-code-group>

There is no `async` in a wasm build: under a `wasm32` target or
`--profile wasi` an `async` function is NL2652.

<scalar-detail title="Under `--emit-ts`">

`nish:async` is `nish/runtime/async.mjs`: `awaitAll`
is `Promise.all` over its calls, and `spawn` starts its task without
awaiting it and keeps it, for the launcher to wait on before it exits. The
output resumes in Node's order, not the native one.

</scalar-detail>

Rules: https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/docs/LANGUAGE.md#async-functions-async-and-await

## Functions

### awaitAll

Wait for two calls at once. It is awaited into one name per call,
`const [a, b] = await awaitAll(...)`; one call, or an `awaitAll` not so
destructured, is NL2647.

```ts
function awaitAll<A, B>(
  a: Promise<A>,
  b: Promise<B>,
): Promise<[A, B]>
```

<scalar-field name="a" type="Promise&lt;A&gt;" required>

The first direct call to an `async` function.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="b" type="Promise&lt;B&gt;" required>

The next direct call to an `async` function.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;[A, B]&gt;">

The answers, in the order the calls are written.

</scalar-field>

### cancel

Cancel a task: every `sleep`, `readable` or `writable` it is waiting on
answers `false` at once, and so does every one it makes later, so it runs
on to its end, its `using` bindings dispose and its region is freed. A
task is never stopped in the middle of its code. Refused under
`--emit-ts` (NL4018).

```ts
function cancel(task: i64): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="task" type="i64" required>

A handle `taskId()` answered.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` while the task is still running, so it is now cancelled
  (a second `cancel` of it answers `true` too); `false` for a task that
  has finished, or for `main`.

</scalar-field>

### cancelAfter

Cancel a task `ms` milliseconds from now, unless it finishes first. A
later call replaces the deadline; a negative `ms` removes it. Refused
under `--emit-ts` (NL4018).

```ts
function cancelAfter(task: i64, ms: i32): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="task" type="i64" required>

A handle `taskId()` answered.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ms" type="i32" required>

The milliseconds until the task is cancelled.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` when the task is still running and the deadline is set
  (or removed); `false` for a task that has finished or is `main`.

</scalar-field>

### cancelled

Whether the running task has been cancelled. Refused under `--emit-ts`
(NL4018).

```ts
function cancelled(): boolean
```

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

`true` once `cancel` was called on it, or its `cancelAfter`
  deadline passed.

</scalar-field>

### readable

Suspend the task until `fd` has bytes to read, or its peer has hung up,
while the executor runs the others. Written only as
`await readable(fd)` inside an `async` function (NL2671). Refused under
`--emit-ts` (NL4017).

```ts
function readable(fd: i32): Promise<boolean>
```

<scalar-field name="fd" type="i32" required>

An open descriptor: a socket, a pipe or a terminal.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;boolean&gt;">

`true` once `fd` is ready; `false` when the wait could not be
  made (an `fd` that is not open). A regular file is always ready.

</scalar-field>

### readableWithin

Suspend the task until `fd` has bytes to read, or its peer has hung up,
or `ms` milliseconds pass, whichever comes first. Written only as
`await readableWithin(fd, ms)` inside an `async` function (NL2671).
Refused under `--emit-ts` (NL4018).

```ts
function readableWithin(
  fd: i32,
  ms: i32,
): Promise<boolean>
```

<scalar-field name="fd" type="i32" required>

An open descriptor: a socket, a pipe or a terminal.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ms" type="i32" required>

The most milliseconds to wait; a negative `ms` waits without a
  limit, as `readable` does.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;boolean&gt;">

`true` once `fd` is ready; `false` when `ms` passed first, when
  the wait could not be made, or when the task is cancelled.

</scalar-field>

### sleep

Suspend the task for `ms` milliseconds while the executor runs the
others. Written only as `await sleep(ms)` inside an `async` function
(NL2671).

```ts
function sleep(ms: i32): Promise<boolean>
```

<scalar-field name="ms" type="i32" required>

The milliseconds to wait, an `i32`.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;boolean&gt;">

`true` once the time has passed; `false` at once for a negative
  `ms`, which makes no wait.

</scalar-field>

### spawn

Start `task` as a task of its own and go on without waiting for it. It
runs at once until it first waits on the outside world, then `spawn`
returns; a task that never waits has finished before `spawn` returns.

```ts
function spawn(task: Promise<void>): void
```

<scalar-field name="task" type="Promise&lt;void&gt;" required>

A direct call to an `async` function (NL2644). Nothing reads
  its answer, so it answers `void` or a `Result` it reports itself
  (NL2646).

</scalar-field>

### taskId

The running task's handle, to hand to `cancel` or `cancelAfter`. `main`'s
handle is 0, which no call cancels. Refused under `--emit-ts` (NL4018).

```ts
function taskId(): i64
```

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i64">

The handle, an `i64` that names this task and no later one.

</scalar-field>

### writable

Suspend the task until `fd` takes bytes without blocking, while the
executor runs the others. Written only as `await writable(fd)` inside an
`async` function (NL2671). Refused under `--emit-ts` (NL4017).

```ts
function writable(fd: i32): Promise<boolean>
```

<scalar-field name="fd" type="i32" required>

An open descriptor: a socket, a pipe or a terminal.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;boolean&gt;">

`true` once `fd` is ready; `false` when the wait could not be
  made (an `fd` that is not open). A regular file is always ready.

</scalar-field>

### writableWithin

Suspend the task until `fd` takes bytes without blocking, or `ms`
milliseconds pass, whichever comes first. Written only as
`await writableWithin(fd, ms)` inside an `async` function (NL2671).
Refused under `--emit-ts` (NL4018).

```ts
function writableWithin(
  fd: i32,
  ms: i32,
): Promise<boolean>
```

<scalar-field name="fd" type="i32" required>

An open descriptor: a socket, a pipe or a terminal.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="ms" type="i32" required>

The most milliseconds to wait; a negative `ms` waits without a
  limit, as `writable` does.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="returns" type="Promise&lt;boolean&gt;">

`true` once `fd` is ready; `false` when `ms` passed first, when
  the wait could not be made, or when the task is cancelled.

</scalar-field>
